where: Section 2 (white noise PSD) and Quiz Q5 answer
problem: Unit mismatch. The chapter defines all PSDs as power per rad/s and computes power with (1/2π)∫S(ω)dω. It then writes S_X(ω) = N₀/2 'for every ω' while saying N₀ is in power per Hz. The two-sided density in W/Hz is N₀/2, but converting to rad/s divides by 2π, so the per-rad/s two-sided density is N₀/(4π). Using N₀/2 in the rad/s formula overstates the power by 2π.
fix: Write: 'White noise has a flat two-sided PSD. In power per rad/s it is S_X(ω) = N₀/(4π), where N₀ is the one-sided PSD in power per Hz (the two-sided density per Hz is N₀/2).' Then state the filtered result as S_Y(ω) = |H(ω)|² N₀/(4π), and in Quiz Q5 write S_Y(ω) = |H₁(ω)|²|H₂(ω)|² N₀/(4π).

problem: Calling h(u) 'the gain applied to the input u seconds earlier' is loose: h(u) is a density, and the weight attached to X(t−u) is h(u)du, not h(u). With h having units of 1/s the word 'gain' is misleading.
fix: 'h(u) is the impulse-response weight at lag u; the input u seconds earlier is weighted by h(u)du, so h has units of 1/s when input and output share units.'
